root_cause: The division operation "x / 10" does not behave properly for negative numbers. It can give unexpected results when the input is negative. For example, if `x` is `-9`, the division `-9 / 10` will result in `-0.9`, and converting it to an int will result in `0`, which is not the expected behavior.
suggestion:
Suggestion 1. Avoiding Float Division for Negative Numbers Update the code to use integer division (//) for both branches, ensuring consistent handling for negative numbers.
```java
x = int(input())

if x % 10 == 0:
  print(x // 10)  // Use integer division to handle both positive and negative numbers correctly
else:
  print(x // 10 + 1)
```
